text:
alex: quick Q — where's the best place to grab per-route KV/prefix cache hit-rate panels? I'm trying to tune alerts for a canary that dipped this morning

maria: the Grafana folder is here: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/kv-prefetch/kv-prefetch-overview

maria: panels you want: \u2014 'kv: prefix hit rate (by route)' and 'kv: prefix miss samples'

sam: for logs, Loki -> labels: job=kv-prefetch service=kv-store , then filter by route: {route="/v1/chat"} and look for "prefetch_miss"

alex: thanks. any suggested alert thresholds? our current alert fired at 75% for 5m and it was noisy

priya: suggestion: set a two-tier alert
priya: - warning: route hit-rate < 65% for 10m
priya: - critical: route hit-rate < 50% for 5m
priya: adjust depending on traffic volume (low-qps routes should have longer windows)

maria: also check the sampling panel (prefix length distribution) — short prefixes have lower hit rates by design
maria: if it's a canary, consider a temporary relaxed threshold for that route during rollout :spiral_calendar_pad:

alex: any owner I should ping to change the alert?

sam: ping @priya for the alert change, and @maria for dashboard tweaks. I can help validate the alert firing logic after you update it.

alex: cool. I'll open a PR to the alerts repo and tag you both.

priya: ty. include this in the PR description:
priya: ```
priya: query: sum by(route) (rate(kv_prefetch_hit_total[5m])) / sum by(route) (rate(kv_prefetch_requests_total[5m]))
priya: warning: <0.65 for 10m
priya: critical: <0.5 for 5m
priya: note: exclude routes with avg_qps < 1 (low traffic noise)
priya: ```

deploy-bot: deploy completed for canary/alpha at 2025-11-02T09:33:12Z :white_check_mark:

maria: also linking runbook: https://wiki.redwood.io/runbooks/kv-prefetch-alert — contains troubleshooting steps and playbook for mitigation (cache warmers, rollback)

alex: great, thanks everyone. I'll attach sample logs and a short run of trace spans (jaeger) to the PR for context.

sam: quick tip: when you attach traces, include span tag `kv.route` and `cache_status` so we can correlate misses -> backend latency

alex: will do. closing the loop here :thumbsup:
